result:
The proposed formula fails at r = 2, p = 13.

For r = 2, a triangle-free Cayley graph Cay(Z_p, S) requires S to be sum-free: if x, y, x+y ∈ S, then 0, x, x+y form a triangle. The largest sum-free subset of Z_13 has size 4, since {5,6,7,8} is sum-free and a size-5 set always contains a solution to x+y=z. So |S| ≤ 4, and {±5, ±6} = {5,6,7,8} attains 4. The true value is therefore 4.

The proposed formula gives 12 − 2⌈12/4⌉ = 12 − 6 = 6, which is too large. The formula also has no derivation behind it; the earlier checks at p = 5, 7, 11 agree only by coincidence.

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 5
